rows.what the ink shows: An initial upright and small curled stroke precede a short flattened letter sequence with a separate dot above its later part. No clear tall internal d or separate final de is distinguishable, but the initial letters and joins are too compressed to certify the complete first candidate.

Beneath the diagonal cancellation, a tall loop continues into a descending stem and low hook. A separate short upper-right oblique tick supports the apostrophe; no following baseline letter is visible.

The deleted lower line retains an initial open c and a small terminal oval in its first group, followed by a second group with an initial tall downstroke; thick horizontal cancellation hides the internal joins. The clearly written compte tenu above belongs to the insertion and cannot certify the lower deleted letters.

The deleted cluster has a lower oval and several rising strokes intersected by a dark horizontal cancellation. The loop-to-ascender junction needed to establish d is obscured, and the terminal down/up strokes do not securely isolate u.

Between the equals sign and phi, a dark n-like body and short right upright are crossed by a long rising slash and a low bent return. A factorial dot, numerator and fraction rule cannot be isolated; the radical-like angular contour may itself be cancellation, so the listed alternatives remain unresolved.

The numeral inside the parentheses has a small upper lobe and a larger rounded lower lobe meeting a descending stem. This double-lobed construction supports 8 rather than the single angled construction of 7.
A thick horizontal cancellation covers the baseline; short raised strokes and two narrow terminal arches remain above it, but the intervening letters of naturel cannot be separated.

Immediately after F, a dense oblique black patch absorbs the beginning and middle of the canceled group. A separate dot and a low curve survive toward its right, but they do not establish the letters of dans.
Before the wedge F there is a compact large loop crossed by rising and horizontal strokes, with a hooked descent at its right. The overtracing does not let me distinguish separate s, u, and r bodies.

After est, two separate horizontal strokes precede another small joined group with an initial u cup and a low n shoulder extending rightward. The first group may be an equals sign or an obscured layer, so it remains uncertain; the following un is distinct and visible.

After subsis, two heavy nearly parallel strokes cover the short group and meet upright traces at its two ends. The interior letter bodies cannot be separated well enough to establish tent beneath the cancellation.

A long thick horizontal deletion crosses the word; a descender in its left portion and two later upward strokes remain visible. Most baseline bodies are merged into the deletion, so the full sequence produits is not independently recoverable.
